limitations: The required full stack was not compiled or executed, so immediate and greater-than-one-second duplicate, ghost, and missing values are unknown.
The existing v8 field-level trace was never ASN.1 constrained, UPER encoded, decoded by CPBasicService, or delivered through its callback.
Path 1 proved that the user OpenCV prefix works but exposed an unconditional libcarla to gRPC configure dependency.
Path 2 did not finish the official builder's gRPC source dependency inside the bounded download window; no conclusion about later source compatibility or link success is supported.
No old-new oracle was supplied, but this control alone cannot validate an unexecuted trace.
Remote /tmp artifacts were retained as requested; the fixed repository was not edited.

verdictRationale.reason: Neither allowed dependency path produced libautomotive or ran the mandated ASN.1 decoder-to-callback-to-LDM-to-timeout chain. The candidate therefore cannot receive a go verdict from this execution gate, and the v8 adapter result is insufficient by the stated rules.

publicAssetTwoWeekExecutability.basis: The fixed public repository, ns-3 tag, gRPC tag, ASN.1 sources, Ubuntu packages, and documented Ubuntu 22.04 path are all publicly available. The observed block is dependency provisioning and download completion rather than a missing receiver implementation. A pre-provisioned disposable Ubuntu 22.04 environment following the official dependency contract can reasonably execute this public path within two weeks, but this audit did not demonstrate that execution and makes no performance claim.

nextActions: Keep the candidate at revise and do not use v8 adapter metrics as full-stack evidence.

Only a future rerun in a pre-provisioned Ubuntu 22.04 environment may reopen the gate; it must produce official automotive object hashes and execute the exact ASN.1/CPBasicService/receiveCPM/translateCPMdata/LDM/timeout chain without an old-new oracle.
Do not change the runner, tests, or idea-center from this closure.
